lecons.title: What a set is
lecons.summary: A set is a collection of objects or things that are alike. The objects of a set are called its elements. A set is written inside braces, with its elements separated by commas: A = { 2, 4, 6, 8 }. And n(A) is the number of elements in the set A.

lecons.title: The types of sets
lecons.summary: Sets take their name from what they hold. A unit set has one element only. A finite set can be counted to the end. An infinite set never ends. The empty set has no element at all. And the universal set U holds every element being considered.

explanations.body: One element, and one only. { 7 } is a unit set; { 7, 8 } is not.
A singleton is a house with one person in it. Let a second one in, and it is no longer a singleton.

lecons.title: The signs of sets
lecons.summary: Four signs come back in every exercise. ∈ means is an element of, and ∉ means is not. ⊂ means is a subset of. ∩ is the intersection, what is common, and ∪ is the union, all together. A’ is the complement of A: everything in U that is not in A.

explanations.body: The sentence 2 ∈ A is read: 2 is an element of A.
